findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at class definition time, not per-instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default. Field/parameter defaults in Python are evaluated exactly once, when the class body executes at module import time — not each time an `AssignmentSource` is instantiated. As a result, every `AssignmentSource` created without explicitly passing `queued=` (e.g. via `AssignmentSource.from_integration()`, used throughout `sync.py`) will carry the same frozen timestamp: the moment the module was first imported (e.g. worker startup), not the actual time the assignment was queued. This silently defeats the purpose of the `queued` field for any logging/debugging/TTL use and is a classic Python footgun that should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: `queued` datetime is not safely round-tripped through task serialization
findings.body: `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a raw `datetime` object. This dict is passed verbatim as Celery task kwargs (`assignment_source_dict`) in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py`). If the task broker uses JSON serialization, the `datetime` will be converted to an ISO string on the wire, but `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` (line 30-35) does not convert it back into a `datetime` when reconstructing the object — it just passes the raw dict through `cls(**input_dict)`. This leaves `queued` as a `str` on the consumer side instead of the declared `datetime` type, which can raise exceptions or silently misbehave wherever `queued` is later treated as a datetime. No test exercises the actual serialize/deserialize round trip through the task boundary, so this discrepancy is not caught.

findings.title: No test verifying cross-integration assignment sources still sync outward
findings.body: The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only verifies that outbound sync is suppressed when the `assignment_source` integration matches the target integration. There is no corresponding test confirming the stated complementary behavior — that when `assignment_source` refers to a *different* integration than the one being synced to, the outbound sync still fires (per the comment in `issues.py`: "This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward"). Without this test, a regression that accidentally suppresses all outbound syncs whenever any `assignment_source` is present would go undetected.

findings.title: `assignment_source` parameter added to `sync_status_outbound` abstract method is unused
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature now accepts `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, mirroring the assignee-sync fix, but nothing in this PR actually threads an `AssignmentSource` into a `should_sync` cycle-break check for status syncing (unlike `sync_assignee_outbound`, where `should_sync('outbound_assignee', parsed_assignment_source)` is called). No caller in the diff passes a real value for this parameter, so it is effectively dead/unused, and the status-sync equivalent of the issue this PR claims to fix (repeated inbound/outbound status webhooks causing sync loops) is not actually addressed despite the API surface suggesting it is.

findings.title: Typo in test method name
findings.body: `test_from_dict_inalid_data` misspells "invalid", which can make the test harder to find/search for and reads as unintentional sloppiness in new test code; should be `test_from_dict_invalid_data`.
